messages:
raj: Heads-up — starting onboarding for titanus-44b today. Weights are staged at s3://redwood-models/titanus-44b/v1/ . Can infra/runtime folks sanity-check checksums and confirm the serve config lint? @anya saw some odd BPE splits on Cyrillic in the eval set, tagging you for tokenizer checks. Quick checklist in message below.

raj: config snippet I'm proposing (small edits welcome):
```
model: titanus-44b
weights_path: s3://redwood-models/titanus-44b/v1/
batch_size: 32
max_seq_len: 2048
rope: { type: "dynamic", base: 10000, scale: 0.5 }
attention_impl: fused_flash_attn
kv_prefetch: true
sliding_window: { size: 1024, stride: 768 }
gqa_groups: 8
```

maria: Quick answer — I pulled the bucket, checksums for all 8 shards match the manifest except shard-06.bin is 0.2% smaller. Re-upload in progress, ETA ~15m. Also the model manifest is missing an explicit tokenizer hash field, can we add that?

anya: Tokenizer note: I ran the eval prompt set and saw Cyrillic splitting into single-letter tokens for common words (example below). Suspect BPE vocab mapping offset due to a different normalization in the repo we used to generate vocab.
Input: "Привет, как дела?"
Tokens: ["П","ри","в","ет",","," \u200b","к","а","к"," \u200b","д","е","л","а","?"]
That \u200b entries look like zero-width spaces from a preprocessing step. If the tokenizer used NFKC vs NFC during vocab generation we'll see drift. I can add a lightweight normalize step in tokenizer init to strip ZWSP and force NFC.

kevin: Re: runtime bits — two quick flags to watch: the sliding_window.size of 1024 with stride 768 will push KV cache counts high for long multi-turn sessions. If the default kv_store per-core is small we might OOM on busy hosts. Suggest either lower window to 896 or increase kv_store.shards. Also fused_flash_attn on A100 driver 525+ is okay, but for older nodes fallback to cuDNN path. Add an explicit attention_fallback list.

kevin: Also, rope.scale=0.5 in dynamic mode looks fine but double-check the model's rope_exponent that the exporter used. We've had mismatches where exported weights assumed legacy RoPE scaling and runtime used linear scaling which caused context drift after ~1k tokens. Small test: run the rollout with a short generated sequence and compare logits at step 512 and 1024.

raj: Thanks — I'll wait for shard reupload then push tokenizer hash into the manifest. On RoPE: can someone run the small logistic test you mentioned? I can run the eval harness once shard-06 is back.

ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: titanus-44b v1 -> infra-canary-3 at 2360128000, duration 20m, traffic=5%. Logs will post to #eng-runtime/canary.

maria: shard-06 re-upload complete and manifest updated with tokenizer_hash: sha256:9f8a3b... I also bumped kv_store.shards=4 on the canary hosts per kevin's suggestion. :thumbsup:

anya: I pushed a small tokenizer patch to handle ZWSP and normalization. Test cases added for Cyrillic. Patch PR: <https://git.internal/redwood/tokenizers/pulls/1427|tokenizer PR 1427> — please review, it's tiny.

kevin: Reviewing infra changes. I also pushed an attention_fallback list to the serve config and added a preflight check that runs a 1k token generation and compares logits to a reference snapshot (tolerance 1e-4). PR: <https://git.internal/redwood/serve-config/pulls/359|serve-config PR 359>. Can someone from runtime approve so we can flip the canary when ready?

raj: I'll run the preflight once tokenizer PR is merged and shard checksum looks good. If preflight is green we go canary -> monitor 20m -> 20% traffic ramp.

maria: Preflight ran against canary at 2360128018 — small divergence at token 1024 but within tolerance. No OOMs observed during 30m warmup.

raj: Awesome, merging the onboarding checklist now and pinging for final reviews. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround :eyes: :thumbsup:
